payload.explanation: Monitor stat_base1 (stationarity, agent-chosen epsilon=0.005m used only to trigger detection since base1 carries no contract/tolerance) fired during place_u_brown at a peak departure of 0.0065m from its arm-time reference position (0.402780,-0.198567,0.022379). get_evidence over the surrounding window (object_poses for base1 and u_brown) shows base1 was static to floating-point precision for ~1s beforehand, then as u_brown descended from z=0.095m to its seated height around wall_ns 1.7920340009e18-1.7920340015e18, base1's pose transiently jumped (peak offset 0.0065m, with a correlated orientation tilt), then settled into a new stable pose (0.401852,-0.199084,0.022379, yaw quaternion z=0.00128) that persisted unchanged for the remainder of the step and beyond (confirmed static at wall_ns ~1.792034036e18). Net persistent displacement from the original reference is ~0.0011m with a ~0.15° yaw change. The zero-jitter baseline readings rule out sensor noise as the explanation; this is a real, if small, physical bump of the fixture caused by contact during u_brown's seating. Per the task spec, base1 is acted upon (contact expected) but must not be displaced, and it was not picked (satisfying that half of the invariant) but its resting pose did shift measurably and permanently. I judge this a genuine, small-magnitude violation of the fixture's "must not be displaced" requirement rather than a mis-arming, since the shift is real and persistent, not an artifact of my threshold choice. No contract clause/tolerance exists for base1 to size this against, so I report it as an instruction-level finding (clause_id null) with the observed magnitude stated plainly.

payload.explanation: Monitor slip_u_brown-pattern monitor slip_line_green (relative_frame, tcp vs line_green, max_delta_m=0.02 sourced and verified from raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m) fired while line_green was still held, before release, during the precision lower-and-seat motion of place_line_green. get_evidence over the surrounding window shows: the TCP frame's orientation was essentially static throughout (quaternion x~0.99997, constant to 5 decimal places) while line_green's orientation rotated substantially and monotonically (quaternion x component moved from -0.114 to -0.222, roughly a 20+ degree reorientation) before stabilizing. Over the same interval the TCP descended from world z=0.158 to z=0.128 (30mm) while line_green's own height only dropped from z=0.083 to z=0.075 (8mm) and then held flat -- the object's vertical motion decoupled from the gripper's. This is consistent with line_green making first contact with the fixture/neighboring part and tipping/settling in the gripper's jaws while the gripper continued its planned descent, rather than tracking rigidly. Grasp width was unchanged since the grasp phase (0.0258m throughout, no re-grip), so this is not the documented TCP-offset artifact from a width change; the shift is a real relative displacement between the held part and the gripper. The observed peak departure (0.0207m) exceeds the contract-sourced grasp_slip_tolerance_m of 0.02m, so I judge this a genuine, if narrow, violation of the in-hand-slippage invariant: the part moved relative to the gripper before it was released.

At end_step the executor itself reported claimed_outcome="failure" for place_line_green, with final_position 0.0227m from line_green_placement (exceeding the raw_spec.tolerances.position_m=0.015m bound) and an orientation error of 25.75 degrees (exceeding raw_spec.tolerances.orientation_deg=10), noting the part appeared tipped/misseated. This independently corroborates the in-hand-slippage finding I already recorded for this same step (slip_line_green fired at 0.0207m, just over the 0.02m grasp_slip_tolerance_m, during the final lower-and-seat motion): the part tipped/rotated in the gripper's grasp during approach, then was set down at the wrong height and orientation rather than seated at its placement frame. This is a second, distinct clause failure (the effects pose/orientation requirement, separate from the slippage invariant) discovered at this step's own end_step evidence, so it is recorded as its own finding under the same step_id. The executor has since opened an unplanned step reseat_line_green (object_ids line_green, u_brown, u_orange) attempting a recovery, which I am now tracking; final conformance for line_green will be re-measured at whatever step closes its corrected placement.

payload.explanation: Monitor stat_base1_v2 (stationarity, agent-chosen epsilon=0.005m used only for trigger detection; base1 has no contract or tolerance of its own) fired during the unplanned reseat_line_green step (not on the expected process map, named here as unplanned; it is a recovery re-pick/re-seat of line_green after place_line_green's tip-over failure). get_evidence over the surrounding window shows base1 static to floating-point precision beforehand (0.402180,-0.200572,0.022392), then undergoing a transient excursion while line_green -- which was resting tipped on/near base1 after the earlier failed placement -- was picked back up, and settling into a clearly new, stable pose at (0.412995,-0.194525,0.022379) with a persistent yaw rotation (quaternion z changed from ~0.002 to -0.0620, roughly 7 degrees). Net persistent displacement from the prior reference is approximately 0.0124m with a ~7-degree rotation, both well beyond measurement noise (readings are bit-exact when undisturbed) and an order of magnitude larger than the earlier, smaller place_u_brown contact bump. This is consistent with line_green (tipped partly onto or against base1) being dragged against the fixture as the gripper closed and lifted it during the recovery re-pick. Per the task specification base1 is acted upon by contact but must never be displaced; this disturbance is real, substantial, and persists, so I judge it a genuine violation rather than sensor artifact or mis-arming.

payload.explanation: Monitor stat_u_brown_seated (stationarity, armed against u_brown's absolute world position right after its own place step closed; threshold from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m=0.02, sourced and verified) fired during the unplanned reseat_line_green step, with u_brown having drifted ~0.016-0.02m in absolute world position and rotated noticeably (quaternion y/z components grew from near-zero to ~0.045-0.086) while no step named or acted on u_brown. get_evidence shows this was not a new, independent contact: u_brown_placement itself shifted by almost the same vector and rotation over the same interval (from (0.401728,-0.151384,0.045379) right after place_u_brown to (0.418897,-0.147185,0.045379) now, with orientation rotating from near-identity to the same ~0.044 y/z quaternion components), closely tracking base1's own already-recorded displacement during this step. This indicates u_brown_placement is defined relative to base1 and that u_brown, resting on base1, was carried along rigidly when the fixture was bumped during the re-pick of line_green. Checked against its own (co-moved) placement frame at this same instant, u_brown is only 0.0022m away -- well within the 0.01m position tolerance -- so u_brown's own seating remains correct in the frame that actually governs its effects clause; the literal instruction-level "stay in its absolute resting pose until acted on" invariant did register a real, non-trivial absolute displacement, so I record it as a finding, but it is the downstream propagation of the base1 disturbance already recorded for this step, not a separate incident, and does not by itself put u_brown's final seating at risk.

clause.text: u_brown re-armed at its current (base1-co-moved) resting pose after confirmed downstream disturbance

payload.explanation: Monitor slip_line_green_v3 (relative_frame, tcp vs line_green, threshold 0.02m sourced/verified from raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m) fired during the second re-seat attempt within reseat_line_green, at 0.0211m departure, just over threshold. This is consistent with the end_step claim for this same step (claimed_outcome failure, position_error_m 0.0318 vs 0.015 tolerance, orientation ~45 degrees off vs 10 degree tolerance, part tipped again): line_green slipped/rotated in the gripper during this second precision placement attempt as well, the same failure mode as the first attempt, and was again set down away from its placement frame. I separately note, without recording a verdict for it, that a monitor_fire from effort_u_brown (triggering_value 114.34 vs threshold 100) occurred earlier in this step while the gripper was actually holding line_green, not u_brown (u_brown had already been placed and released). That monitor remained armed on the shared finger_joint continuously after u_brown was released, so the fire reflects line_green's grip effort compared against u_brown's clamp-effort bound -- a mis-arming on my part, not a physical violation of u_brown's invariant, since u_brown was not being gripped at that time. I am not re-arming an unconditional finger_joint effort monitor against a per-object threshold going forward.

At end_step the executor reported claimed_outcome="failure" for reseat_line_green, with line_green's final position 0.0318m from line_green_placement (exceeding raw_spec.tolerances.position_m=0.015m) and an orientation roughly 45 degrees off (quaternion qy=-0.39), far outside raw_spec.tolerances.orientation_deg=10. This is the same tip-over failure mode seen in the first place_line_green attempt, now recurring on the recovery attempt as well, and corroborates the slip_line_green_v3 finding recorded for this step. The run then ended (run_ended status=aborted) with line_green left unseated, tipped roughly 45 degrees near but not at its placement frame.

This is the run's final end-state verdict. I measured each part's current pose against its own placement frame directly via query_snapshot rather than trusting the executor's claims: u_brown is 0.00205m from u_brown_placement (well within 0.01m) and u_orange is 0.00191m from u_orange_placement (well within 0.02m) -- both remain correctly seated, including after base1_placement-frame co-movement from the base1 disturbances recorded mid-run (two findings: a small ~0.0011m bump during place_u_brown, and a larger ~0.0124m/7-degree shift during reseat_line_green). Those base1 disturbances propagated kinematically to u_brown/u_orange's absolute poses and placement frames together (both are evidently defined relative to base1), which is why u_brown's own stationarity monitor also fired (recorded as a finding) even though u_brown's seating relative to its own placement frame never left tolerance. line_green, by contrast, stands uncorrected at run end: its final pose is 0.0301m from line_green_placement with a roughly 45-degree orientation error, both far outside the 0.015m / 10-degree tolerances, after two separate place attempts (place_line_green, then the unplanned recovery step reseat_line_green, named here as unplanned) both ended in a tip-over, each corroborated by an in-hand-slippage monitor fire just over the 0.02m threshold during the final lowering motion. inverted_u_yellow was never reached: pick_inverted_u_yellow/place_approach_inverted_u_yellow/place_inverted_u_yellow never began (run_ended status=aborted after the second line_green failure), so inverted_u_yellow has no attempted end-state and remains at its original resting pose. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) measured at run end are bit-identical to their run-start reference poses, confirming the bystander stationarity invariant held throughout despite two carried-part/fixture contact events elsewhere on the table. One monitor fire (effort_u_brown, 114.34 vs threshold 100) is excluded from clause_results as mis-armed: it fired while the gripper held line_green, not u_brown, because the monitor continued watching the shared finger_joint under u_brown's clamp threshold after u_brown had already been released -- a fact about my monitor design, not a physical violation. Because line_green's misseated, uncorrected end-state is a standing violation, the run's end-state verdict is non_conformant: this outranks the incomplete status that would otherwise apply to inverted_u_yellow's untouched state, per the verdict-precedence rule (a standing violation wins regardless of how the run stopped).
